jobs.title: Senior AI Engineer
jobs.description:
About Us

At Provectus
, you don’t prototype in a sandbox and hand a client a slide deck. You embed inside a bank, an insurer, or a health system, learn the work, and ship a Claude + AWS system into their real, regulated production — then you watch the business number move. We’re an Anthropic and AWS Partner with 150+ certified architects. That means the newest models, real budgets, and problems that matter — without the layers, politics, and years-to-impact of a hundred-thousand-person firm. 350+ builders, 100+ customers in production, founder-led since 2010, offices across North America, LATAM, and EMEA.

Why Provectus

Frontier access — Anthropic Preferred Partner: newest Claude models, real budgets, real problems.
Real tasks (not scope), real deployment. You go where the operating problem is and ship production code to real users, not slide decks that sit in a drive.
Embedded, not engaged. You are part of the customer’s team and inside their process — not a vendor running a project alongside it. Embedded is not staff-augmented.
Autonomous. You own the work from framing through to production, visible to clients and founders. You own the method; nobody hands you a ticket.
Your experience stays portable. Every engagement is a new problem, often in a new industry, so your skills compound instead of narrowing to one product. No legacy-maintenance grind, not a single stack.
Craft & growth — build beside senior FDEs on a Claude-certified team; a real platform (talks, OSS) to grow your name.
We give you a stage: Claude certification, conference talks, open-source contributions, published work under your own name.

What you’ll do:

Spend the first weeks of each engagement in the operator’s seat, learning the constraints from the inside, then rebuild the function from first principles alongside the client and a Forward Deployed Executive — and you are the one who builds it.
Be part of the customer’s team, inside their process; work on real tasks, not scoped deliverables, and own the method autonomously.
You won’t start from zero. Provectus builds industry Blueprints — working systems that have already shipped for a customer in your industry. Your engagement starts from that baseline, and what you learn in the field goes back into it.
Deliver across Cowork Activation, Agentic SDLC, and Blueprint Activations in Financial Services and Healthcare.
Help shape how leading enterprises adopt AI, from strategy through first deployment; help build the tooling and frameworks of a growing AI delivery practice.

What we look for:

Typically 7+ years building software, a substantial share of it writing production code you were accountable for. You are hands-on today and intend to stay that way.
Genuinely willing to spend time understanding someone else’s job before writing code; demonstrated ability to become conversant in an unfamiliar business function quickly.
Shipped GenAI/LLM systems to production — not demos, not notebooks. You’ve handled the parts that get hard after the prototype works.
You evaluate. You have built or owned an eval suite for a non-deterministic system, and you can explain what you measured and why.
Strong engineering fundamentals — dropped into an unfamiliar codebase or language, you’re productive. Python and/or TypeScript proficiency; depth matters more than stack.
Cloud-native delivery on AWS (GCP/Azure a plus), including the operational reality of a system someone else inherits.
Pre-sales experience. Credible with senior stakeholders — you can hold a redesign conversation with a BU head and a scoping conversation with a CTO without losing either room.
Comfort with ambiguity and ownership. Engagements start underspecified by design. Closing that gap is the job.
Hands-on experience with Claude, Claude Code, and Cowork (skills, workflows, MCP, integrations, connectors, custom harnesses).

Nice to have:

Containers and orchestration (Kubernetes/ECS) and CI/CD in production.
IaC depth: AWS CDK, CloudFormation, Terraform.
Open-source contributions or public writing on applied AI.

What we offer:

Full-time.
On-site visits to client’s facilities and our office in NYC 1/week
Unlimited Vacation policy.
Generous health, vision, and dental insurance.
401(K) matching plan.
Base salary $180k–$200k + bonuses; OTE up to $250k. The salary range is determined through interviews and a review of the education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities of the applicant, and alignment with market data.
No Visa sponsorship

We’re real

A person reads your application. We filter out AI-generated and fraudulent submissions automatically. Every application that clears that filter is read by someone on our team.
We may ask for a quick ID verification. Fraudulent applications are common, and this protects real candidates.
You’ll meet the people you’d work with. We host AI engineering events in New York and San Francisco. We'd be happy to talk in person. Your interviews are with Pavel Borobov, Solutions Architect, and Stepan Pushkarev, Co-Founder & CEO.

How we hire:

Recruitment interview.
Tech interview with our FDE (30 min).
A live engineering building session (1.5 hours). We hand you a business function and the constraints. You have to understand the job and rebuild it — then say what you’d build and how you’d know it worked. Use AI the way you normally would; we expect AI-generated code. What we look at is how you used AI, the judgment behind your choices, and what you researched beyond what any LLM already knows.
Soft skills interview.
Offer discussion.

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

Instructional Designer, AI-Enabled Learning

Global Commercial Learning & Capability Transformation

About The Team

Our global sales force is the worldwide infrastructure that gets our medicines to underserved patients, and our Commercial Learning & Capability Transformation team ensures our people have the skills, confidence, and tools to make that happen.

We are building a future-ready learning ecosystem that blends science, creativity, and technology to elevate the capability of every commercial team member, everywhere in the world. Our vision is to be the most innovative commercial learning team in biopharma, using AI-powered learning experiences to set a new standard for how our people learn and perform.

About The Role

We are seeking a contract Instructional Designer with a strong aptitude for AI-enabled learning tools to help bring this ecosystem to life.

In this role, you will leverage our AI-enabled learning technology stack to create learning experiences that are engaging, memorable, and built for retention. You will develop micro-learnings, AI practice simulations, and courses using our learning experience platform, Sana Labs, and other AI-enabled tools, and every program you build will be designed to meet our compliance standards. You will partner with business stakeholders to understand what is driving performance needs and work closely with our learning leads to focus on the initiatives with the greatest business impact. As needed, you will also provide coordination support for live and virtual learning programs.

This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys building, experimenting, and seeing their work make a measurable difference in the field.

Design learning that is engaging, memorable, and effective

Design for retention, applying techniques such as spaced practice, retrieval, scenario-based learning, and reinforcement so learners can recall and apply what they've learned long after initial training
Partner with SMEs to translate disease-state and product knowledge into clear, engaging, and actionable learning experiences
Stay current on emerging AI tools and approaches, and pilot new ideas that improve speed, quality, and learner engagement while maintaining compliance standards
Ensure every program is compliant
Develop all training in accordance with applicable regulatory, legal, and company requirements, building compliance into the design from the start
Manage learning programs through the Medical, Legal, and Regulatory (MLR) review process, from initial submission through final approval
Prepare content and supporting references for review, track feedback, incorporate revisions, and keep projects on schedule
Maintain accurate training materials, approvals, and documentation so that all learning is audit-ready
Manage course assignments and content uploads in our learning experience platform and help troubleshoot learner completion issues.
Lead with discovery and business partnership
Meet with business stakeholders to understand capability gaps, field needs, and desired outcomes
Translate those insights into clear learning solutions and development plans
Work in close coordination with team leads to prioritize projects and align on scope, timelines, and success measures
Collaborate with global learning colleagues to share ideas and reuse successful approaches across therapeutic areas and regions
Support live and virtual learning
Provide coordination support for live and virtual learning programs as needed, including logistics, materials, scheduling, and facilitation support
Help ensure every session runs smoothly for learners and facilitators

What You'll Bring

Required

7+ years of instructional design experience, ideally in a commercial, sales training, or life sciences setting
Strong aptitude for AI-enabled learning tools, with hands-on experience using them to design and build learning (Rise, Articulate 360, Sana Labs, Arist or Synthesia experience is a plus)
Hands-on experience building micro-learnings, simulations, and e-learning in a learning experience platform
Demonstrated experience managing content through MLR or a comparable compliance review process, and a strong understanding of the importance of compliant, audit-ready training
A track record of designing engaging learning that drives retention and application, not just completion
Working knowledge of assigning and uploading content in an LMS or learning experience platform, and troubleshooting learner completion issues.
Comfort leading stakeholder discovery and translating business needs into learning solutions
Strong project management and communication skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects independently
A growth mindset and enthusiasm for learning new tools quickly and sharing what works with the team
Ability to work effectively in a global, cross-functional environment

Preferred

Rare disease or biopharma commercial training experience
Familiarity with commercial enablement needs, such as launch readiness, onboarding, and field skills development
Experience with authoring tools such as Articulate Storyline, Rise, or similar
Experience coordinating or supporting virtual instructor-led training
Bachelor's degree in instructional design, education, learning and development, or a related field, or equivalent experience

What Success Looks Like

Learning is delivered on time, approved through MLR efficiently, and fully compliant and audit-ready
Programs are aligned to real business priorities and make a measurable difference in the field
Learners enjoy the experience, remember what they learned, and apply it on the job
Stakeholders view you as a trusted partner who understands their needs
You use AI tools to build learning faster and better, and you help the team discover new ways to do the same
Our continuous learning ecosystem becomes more engaging, innovative, and impactful because you were part of it

Principal Machine Learning Engineer

New York, United States

About Us

Re-architecting Engineering for the Age of Intelligence

PhysicsX is the physics AI company for industrials. The company’s mission is to accelerate hardware innovation by overhauling what industrial engineering and manufacturing look like today. PhysicsX is building a new simulation software stack to deliver deep physics AI enablement across the entire engineering lifecycle. The company partners with leading organisations in aerospace & defence, automotive, semiconductors, materials, and energy & renewables, supporting them on some of their most critical and complex challenges. PhysicsX is headquartered in the United Kingdom, with offices in London, New York, and Singapore and an expanding presence in the Bay Area.

Who We're Looking For

As a Principal Machine Learning Engineer in Delivery, you are an experienced problem solver and technical leader who stays anchored to impact. You can grasp advanced engineering concepts across multiple industries, lead technical initiatives, and work directly with customers (often side by side on-site) to embed cutting-edge AI models into tools that are useful and used.

For this role, that means manufacturing and maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO).
You have put ML into production on industrial process or sensor data, not benchmarks. You know the difference between a model that scores well offline and one a process owner will accept on a qualified production line. Your data comes off equipment rather than out of a solver: it is sparse, drifting, miscalibrated and partly unrecorded, and you know how to work with it.

You've shipped ML systems end to end and at scale: you design, build and test reliable, scalable ML data pipelines, select the right libraries, frameworks and tools, and make pragmatic product decisions that set Delivery up for success. Working at the intersection of data science and software engineering, you translate R&D and project outputs into reusable libraries, tooling and products.

With at least 5 years of industry experience (post Masters or PhD) in a commercial, non-research environment, you're ready not only to execute but to lead and mentor others.

This Role

You'll work closely with Data Scientists, Simulation Engineers, Manufacturing Process Experts and customers to define the process and physics problems we are solving, and you'll drive decisions on reliable deployment with measurable outcomes on the shop floor.

You'll

Own the ML approach to manufacturing and MRO data, from modelling through deployment in customer production environments (cloud, on-prem and edge).
Build production ML on sparse, drifting, miscalibrated process and sensor data (process logs, sensor traces, inspection records, small DoE sets), and judge whether the data is enough to train on.
Choose between physics simulation, reduced-order and learned models, and fuse simulation with shop-floor measurement where the two disagree.
Set the UQ and validation standard for what a process recommendation may claim against a qualified process window, and design experiments where machine time is the cost.
Make models transfer across machines, material lots and consumable batches.
Define the product requirements that manufacturing and MRO place on the PhysicsX platform.
Lead scoping and architecture for data and ML systems, and communicate results and trade-offs to senior stakeholders and process owners.
Build end-to-end training and inference pipelines and APIs (Python, PyTorch, Pandas, FastAPI, SciPy, Kubeflow, among others), including for 3D point-cloud and mesh data, and mentor engineers and data scientists.
Travel to customer sites worldwide, on average 3-4 weeks per quarter, and take part in scoping new projects and bringing new customers to PhysicsX.

What you've done

We hire on what you've done, so strong candidates can point to things like:

Built and deployed ML on manufacturing process data (parameter logs, sensor traces, inspection records or small DoE sets) and can say what changed in production as a result
Fused simulation output with shop-floor measurement where the two disagreed
Set UQ and validation standards that other teams followed
Shaped a product or tooling roadmap based on what a site or company actually needed
Had a recommendation rejected by a process owner, and understood why

Experience in aerospace or another regulated manufacturing environment is a plus. It is not required, because the must-have bar can be met in any sector where data comes off equipment.

Our delivery teams drive innovation to turn AI models into practical solutions - read our blog to learn more about how you’ll contribute to this exciting journey!

What We Offer

Build what actually matters

Help shape an AI-native engineering company at a formative stage, tackling problems that genuinely matter for industry and society. This is work with real-world impact - and something you can be proud to stand behind.

Learn alongside exceptional people

Work with a high-caliber, collaborative team of engineers, scientists, and operators who care deeply about doing great work, and about helping each other get better. We come from diverse backgrounds, but we share a commitment to operating at the highest level and addressing some of the most complex challenges out there. If you’re ambitious, thoughtful, and driven by impact, you’ll feel at home.

Influence over hierarchy

We operate with a flat structure: good ideas win - wherever they come from. Questioning assumptions and challenging the status quo isn’t just welcomed, it’s expected.

Sustainable pace, long-term ambition

Building meaningful technology is a marathon, not a sprint. We believe in balancing focused, ambitious work with a life beyond it. Our hybrid model blends time together in our New York office with work-from-home days, giving you the flexibility to work sustainably while staying connected in person.

And it doesn’t stop there …

jobs.description:
About Us

At Provectus
, you don’t prototype in a sandbox and hand a client a slide deck. You embed inside a bank, an insurer, or a health system, learn the work, and ship a Claude + AWS system into their real, regulated production — then you watch the business number move. We’re an Anthropic and AWS Partner with 150+ certified architects. Why Provectus

Frontier access — Anthropic Preferred Partner: newest Claude models, real budgets, real problems.
Real tasks (not scope), real deployment. You go where the operating problem is and ship production code to real users, not slide decks that sit in a drive.
Embedded, not engaged. You are part of the customer’s team and inside their process — not a vendor running a project alongside it. Embedded is not staff-augmented.
Autonomous. You own the work from framing through to production, visible to clients and founders. You own the method; nobody hands you a ticket.
Your experience stays portable. Every engagement is a new problem, often in a new industry, so your skills compound instead of narrowing to one product. No legacy-maintenance grind, not a single stack.
Craft & growth — build beside senior FDEs on a Claude-certified team; a real platform (talks, OSS) to grow your name.
We give you a stage: Claude certification, conference talks, open-source contributions, published work under your own name.

Spend the first weeks of each engagement in the operator’s seat, learning the constraints from the inside, then rebuild the function from first principles alongside the client and a Forward Deployed Executive — and you are the one who builds it.
Be part of the customer’s team, inside their process; work on real tasks, not scoped deliverables, and own the method autonomously.
You won’t start from zero. Provectus builds industry Blueprints — working systems that have already shipped for a customer in your industry. Your engagement starts from that baseline, and what you learn in the field goes back into it.
Deliver across Cowork Activation, Agentic SDLC, and Blueprint Activations in Financial Services and Healthcare.
Help shape how leading enterprises adopt AI, from strategy through first deployment; help build the tooling and frameworks of a growing AI delivery practice.

What we look for:

Typically 7+ years building software, a substantial share of it writing production code you were accountable for. You are hands-on today and intend to stay that way.
Genuinely willing to spend time understanding someone else’s job before writing code; demonstrated ability to become conversant in an unfamiliar business function quickly.
Shipped GenAI/LLM systems to production — not demos, not notebooks. You’ve handled the parts that get hard after the prototype works.
You evaluate. You have built or owned an eval suite for a non-deterministic system, and you can explain what you measured and why.
Strong engineering fundamentals — dropped into an unfamiliar codebase or language, you’re productive. Python and/or TypeScript proficiency; depth matters more than stack.
Cloud-native delivery on AWS (GCP/Azure a plus), including the operational reality of a system someone else inherits.
Pre-sales experience. Credible with senior stakeholders — you can hold a redesign conversation with a BU head and a scoping conversation with a CTO without losing either room.
Comfort with ambiguity and ownership. Engagements start underspecified by design. Closing that gap is the job.
Hands-on experience with Claude, Claude Code, and Cowork (skills, workflows, MCP, integrations, connectors, custom harnesses).

Nice to have:

Containers and orchestration (Kubernetes/ECS) and CI/CD in production.
IaC depth: AWS CDK, CloudFormation, Terraform.
Open-source contributions or public writing on applied AI.

What we offer:

Full-time.
On-site visits to client’s facilities and our office in NYC 1/week
Unlimited Vacation policy.
Generous health, vision, and dental insurance.
401(K) matching plan.
Base salary $180k–$200k + bonuses; OTE up to $250k. The salary range is determined through interviews and a review of the education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities of the applicant, and alignment with market data.
No Visa sponsorship

We’re real

A person reads your application. We filter out AI-generated and fraudulent submissions automatically. Every application that clears that filter is read by someone on our team.
We may ask for a quick ID verification. Fraudulent applications are common, and this protects real candidates.
You’ll meet the people you’d work with. We host AI engineering events in New York and San Francisco. We'd be happy to talk in person. Your interviews are with Pavel Borobov, Solutions Architect, and Stepan Pushkarev, Co-Founder & CEO.

How we hire:

Recruitment interview.
Tech interview with our FDE (30 min).
A live engineering building session (1.5 hours). We hand you a business function and the constraints. You have to understand the job and rebuild it — then say what you’d build and how you’d know it worked. Use AI the way you normally would; we expect AI-generated code. What we look at is how you used AI, the judgment behind your choices, and what you researched beyond what any LLM already knows.
Soft skills interview.
Offer discussion.

These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. Most recently, SecurityScorecard was named to Fast Company’s annual list of the World’s Most Innovative Companies for 2023 and to the Achievers 50 Most Engaged Workplaces in 2023 award recognizing “forward-thinking employers for their unwavering commitment to employee engagement.” SecurityScorecard is proud to be funded by world-class investors including Silver Lake Waterman, Moody’s, Sequoia Capital, GV and Riverwood Capital.

About the Role:

SecurityScorecard is hiring a Principal Software Architect to lead the system design of our agentic AI capabilities and serve as a technical anchor for engineering teams building the next generation of our platform. This is an individual contributor role reporting to the Chief Architect, alongside a Front-end Architect and a Data-focused Architect, and partnering closely with engineering leadership, Product, and Data Science.
We're looking for someone who can go deep technically and also move a room: an architect whose designs get adopted because they're well-reasoned and well-communicated, not just handed down.

You will lead the system design for how agentic features are built, integrated, and operated reliably at production scale, working in close partnership with our Data Science team, who bring the model and ML depth. Your focus is the system: orchestration, state and memory, tool boundaries, failure semantics, and how all of it composes with the wider platform.
Like the rest of our architecture function, you'll prototype to prove out decisions rather than implement full solutions, and you'll set direction through Technical Design Reviews (TDRs), and standards. Deep data-engineering specialization isn't required, but you should be comfortable reasoning about data flows, storage decisions, and how agentic systems consume and act on data.

What You'll Do

Own the system design for our agentic capabilities: orchestration, context and state, tool boundaries, and reliability patterns for non-deterministic systems
Write the TDRs, design docs, and standards that set architectural direction for agentic work across teams
Prototype to validate architectural decisions before teams commit to them at scale
Partner with Data Science so that agent and model work composes cleanly with existing platform services, from APIs and event streaming through to storage
Review TDRs from across engineering, giving teams substantive feedback on architecture and risk, not only on AI work
Build consensus across engineering teams and get them genuinely aligned, not merely compliant
Help drive the shift to AI-assisted and agentic development across engineering, shaping how engineers design, review, and iterate in an AI-native workflow
Mentor senior and staff engineers on agentic system design and measurably elevate the technical bar
Communicate architectural decisions and their trade-offs clearly to executives and customers

Required Qualifications:

10+ years of software engineering experience, including significant time as a senior, staff, or principal-level architect or technical lead designing production systems
Deep expertise in distributed systems: service boundaries, consistency models, event-driven architecture, API design (REST; gRPC familiarity a plus), and operating systems reliably at scale
Hands-on experience building, prototyping, and architecting agentic or LLM-powered systems in production, not just demos: agent loop design, context engineering, MCP and tool/function-calling integration, RAG architectures, memory and state management, and reliability and guardrail patterns for non-deterministic systems
Working knowledge of data engineering fundamentals, including data modeling, pipeline design, and streaming vs. batch, sufficient to make informed architectural calls without deep specialization in the domain
A track record of influence without authority: presenting a technical direction to skeptical engineers and earning genuine buy-in, and giving rigorous design review feedback on systems you didn't build yourself
Strong technical writing and mentorship: TDRs, design docs, and decision records that teams can act on without hand-holding, plus a history of raising the technical bar around you
Ability to communicate complex architectural decisions clearly to executives and customers
Comfort operating as a senior individual contributor, driving outcomes through prototyping and technical credibility

Preferred Qualifications:

Familiarity with multi-agent orchestration patterns (supervisor and sub-agent architectures, agent handoffs), which our use cases are likely to grow toward
Experience with our stack or comparable technologies: Node.js/TypeScript, PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, Kafka, AWS, Kubernetes
Experience leading AI-assisted or agentic development adoption across an engineering organization; given the scope of this work at SecurityScorecard, this carries significant weight
Experience partnering closely with data science or ML teams on productionizing their work
Cybersecurity industry background

Our Tech Stack

Our platform runs on Node.js and TypeScript, with a React Microfrontend Architecture and PostgreSQL and ClickHouse for storage. We use Kafka for event streaming, and our infrastructure runs on AWS with Kubernetes, Terraform, Helm, and ArgoCD. We are actively expanding our AI/ML infrastructure. You do not need to have used every tool here, but you should be comfortable reasoning across a stack of this kind and making principled architectural trade-offs within it.

Benefits:

Specific to each country, we offer a competitive salary, stock options, Health benefits, and unlimited PTO, parental leave, tuition reimbursements, and much more!

new_jobs.description:
About Us

At Provectus
, you don’t prototype in a sandbox and hand a client a slide deck. You embed inside a bank, an insurer, or a health system, learn the work, and ship a Claude + AWS system into their real, regulated production — then you watch the business number move. We’re an Anthropic and AWS Partner with 150+ certified architects. That means the newest models, real budgets, and problems that matter — without the layers, politics, and years-to-impact of a hundred-thousand-person firm. 350+ builders, 100+ customers in production, founder-led since 2010, offices across North America, LATAM, and EMEA.

Why Provectus

Frontier access — Anthropic Preferred Partner: newest Claude models, real budgets, real problems.
Real tasks (not scope), real deployment. You go where the operating problem is and ship production code to real users, not slide decks that sit in a drive.
Embedded, not engaged. You are part of the customer’s team and inside their process — not a vendor running a project alongside it. Embedded is not staff-augmented.
Autonomous. You own the work from framing through to production, visible to clients and founders. You own the method; nobody hands you a ticket.
Your experience stays portable. Every engagement is a new problem, often in a new industry, so your skills compound instead of narrowing to one product. No legacy-maintenance grind, not a single stack.
Craft & growth — build beside senior FDEs on a Claude-certified team; a real platform (talks, OSS) to grow your name.
We give you a stage: Claude certification, conference talks, open-source contributions, published work under your own name.

What you’ll do:

Spend the first weeks of each engagement in the operator’s seat, learning the constraints from the inside, then rebuild the function from first principles alongside the client and a Forward Deployed Executive — and you are the one who builds it.
Be part of the customer’s team, inside their process; work on real tasks, not scoped deliverables, and own the method autonomously.
You won’t start from zero. Provectus builds industry Blueprints — working systems that have already shipped for a customer in your industry. Your engagement starts from that baseline, and what you learn in the field goes back into it.
Deliver across Cowork Activation, Agentic SDLC, and Blueprint Activations in Financial Services and Healthcare.
Help shape how leading enterprises adopt AI, from strategy through first deployment; help build the tooling and frameworks of a growing AI delivery practice.

What we look for:

Typically 7+ years building software, a substantial share of it writing production code you were accountable for. You are hands-on today and intend to stay that way.
Genuinely willing to spend time understanding someone else’s job before writing code; demonstrated ability to become conversant in an unfamiliar business function quickly.
Shipped GenAI/LLM systems to production — not demos, not notebooks. You’ve handled the parts that get hard after the prototype works.
You evaluate. You have built or owned an eval suite for a non-deterministic system, and you can explain what you measured and why.
Strong engineering fundamentals — dropped into an unfamiliar codebase or language, you’re productive. Python and/or TypeScript proficiency; depth matters more than stack.
Cloud-native delivery on AWS (GCP/Azure a plus), including the operational reality of a system someone else inherits.
Pre-sales experience. Credible with senior stakeholders — you can hold a redesign conversation with a BU head and a scoping conversation with a CTO without losing either room.
Comfort with ambiguity and ownership. Engagements start underspecified by design. Closing that gap is the job.
Hands-on experience with Claude, Claude Code, and Cowork (skills, workflows, MCP, integrations, connectors, custom harnesses).

Nice to have:

Containers and orchestration (Kubernetes/ECS) and CI/CD in production.
IaC depth: AWS CDK, CloudFormation, Terraform.
Open-source contributions or public writing on applied AI.

What we offer:

Full-time.
On-site visits to client’s facilities and our office in NYC 1/week
Unlimited Vacation policy.
Generous health, vision, and dental insurance.
401(K) matching plan.
Base salary $180k–$200k + bonuses; OTE up to $250k. The salary range is determined through interviews and a review of the education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities of the applicant, and alignment with market data.
No Visa sponsorship

We’re real

A person reads your application. We filter out AI-generated and fraudulent submissions automatically. Every application that clears that filter is read by someone on our team.
We may ask for a quick ID verification. Fraudulent applications are common, and this protects real candidates.
You’ll meet the people you’d work with. We host AI engineering events in New York and San Francisco. We'd be happy to talk in person. Your interviews are with Pavel Borobov, Solutions Architect, and Stepan Pushkarev, Co-Founder & CEO.

How we hire:

Recruitment interview.
Tech interview with our FDE (30 min).
A live engineering building session (1.5 hours). We hand you a business function and the constraints. You have to understand the job and rebuild it — then say what you’d build and how you’d know it worked. Use AI the way you normally would; we expect AI-generated code. What we look at is how you used AI, the judgment behind your choices, and what you researched beyond what any LLM already knows.
Soft skills interview.
Offer discussion.

These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. Make healthcare #1 in customer service.

(2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024); Deloitte Technology Fast 500

Applicants must be currently authorized and have the ability to provide proof of full-time, long-term authorization to work in the United States. We are unable to provide visa sponsorship or support visa transfers now or in the future.

Artera is hiring a Senior AI Builder to build the agentic systems that deliver exceptional

patient experiences for our customers — scheduling, referral coordination, medication

refills, billing, payment estimation and more.

You'll be a fully contributing builder inside a customer-facing squad bringing AI-native

fluency in delivering end-to-end on your customers’ needs — owning initiatives from

customer discovery through production operation, onboarding new customers onto what

you build, and shipping enhancements that keep pace with the technical possibilities for

a named subset of our provider customers. Your creativity should be boundless, your

desire to deliver world class solutions unmatched, and your initiative and accountability

to those outcomes as a new bar for our customers they themselves aspire to.

At this level, you'll own customer outcomes independently , bringing the curiosity of a

product manager, the discipline of a project manager, and the agentic fluency of an

engineer to your work. You'll develop real subject-matter expertise and long term

relationships with senior healthcare executives, and internally teach and support newer

builders and experiment and advocate for novel agentic techniques that make every

Artera customer even more successful.

Responsibilities

Ownership: Design, build and ship agentic features that handle real patient

conversations end to end, from problem framing through production operation

Strategy: Identify customer pain and create a roadmap for solving their

problems.

Program Management: Own the evaluation story for what you build: define what

good looks like, build the harnesses and test cases yourself, and measure

helpfulness and safety rather than asserting them.

Agentic Development: Build novel solutions for named customers; translate

their operational reality into technical solutions that you yourself architect and

code with our internal agentic systems.

Continuous Improvement: Contribute to our reusable foundations — shared

agent patterns, evaluation tooling and internal libraries — so each new workflow

is faster and safer to build than the last Move quickly on reversible decisions, and

escalate with a proposed course of action when they are not

AI-native: your work across all dimensions will be inherently reliant on AI-native

tools primarily using the CLI; which means you will own a greater breadth and

volume of responsibility than a typical technologist.

Domain Expertise: Operate what you build: participate in on-call for your

surfaces, investigate incidents to root cause, and eliminate recurring classes of

failure rather than individual instances

SecurityScorecard is the global leader in cybersecurity ratings, with over 12 million companies continuously rated, operating in 64 countries. Headquartered in New York City, our culture has been recognized by Inc Magazine as a "Best Workplace,” by Crain’s NY as a "Best Places to Work in NYC," and as one of the 10 hottest SaaS startups in New York for two years in a row. Most recently, SecurityScorecard was named to Fast Company’s annual list of the World’s Most Innovative Companies for 2023 and to the Achievers 50 Most Engaged Workplaces in 2023 award recognizing “forward-thinking employers for their unwavering commitment to employee engagement.” SecurityScorecard is proud to be funded by world-class investors including Silver Lake Waterman, Moody’s, Sequoia Capital, GV and Riverwood Capital.

About the Role:

SecurityScorecard is hiring a Principal Software Architect to lead the system design of our agentic AI capabilities and serve as a technical anchor for engineering teams building the next generation of our platform. This is an individual contributor role reporting to the Chief Architect, alongside a Front-end Architect and a Data-focused Architect, and partnering closely with engineering leadership, Product, and Data Science.
We're looking for someone who can go deep technically and also move a room: an architect whose designs get adopted because they're well-reasoned and well-communicated, not just handed down.

You will lead the system design for how agentic features are built, integrated, and operated reliably at production scale, working in close partnership with our Data Science team, who bring the model and ML depth. Your focus is the system: orchestration, state and memory, tool boundaries, failure semantics, and how all of it composes with the wider platform.
Like the rest of our architecture function, you'll prototype to prove out decisions rather than implement full solutions, and you'll set direction through Technical Design Reviews (TDRs), and standards. Deep data-engineering specialization isn't required, but you should be comfortable reasoning about data flows, storage decisions, and how agentic systems consume and act on data.

What You'll Do

Own the system design for our agentic capabilities: orchestration, context and state, tool boundaries, and reliability patterns for non-deterministic systems
Write the TDRs, design docs, and standards that set architectural direction for agentic work across teams
Prototype to validate architectural decisions before teams commit to them at scale
Partner with Data Science so that agent and model work composes cleanly with existing platform services, from APIs and event streaming through to storage
Review TDRs from across engineering, giving teams substantive feedback on architecture and risk, not only on AI work
Build consensus across engineering teams and get them genuinely aligned, not merely compliant
Help drive the shift to AI-assisted and agentic development across engineering, shaping how engineers design, review, and iterate in an AI-native workflow
Mentor senior and staff engineers on agentic system design and measurably elevate the technical bar
Communicate architectural decisions and their trade-offs clearly to executives and customers

Required Qualifications:

10+ years of software engineering experience, including significant time as a senior, staff, or principal-level architect or technical lead designing production systems
Deep expertise in distributed systems: service boundaries, consistency models, event-driven architecture, API design (REST; gRPC familiarity a plus), and operating systems reliably at scale
Hands-on experience building, prototyping, and architecting agentic or LLM-powered systems in production, not just demos: agent loop design, context engineering, MCP and tool/function-calling integration, RAG architectures, memory and state management, and reliability and guardrail patterns for non-deterministic systems
Working knowledge of data engineering fundamentals, including data modeling, pipeline design, and streaming vs. batch, sufficient to make informed architectural calls without deep specialization in the domain
A track record of influence without authority: presenting a technical direction to skeptical engineers and earning genuine buy-in, and giving rigorous design review feedback on systems you didn't build yourself
Strong technical writing and mentorship: TDRs, design docs, and decision records that teams can act on without hand-holding, plus a history of raising the technical bar around you
Ability to communicate complex architectural decisions clearly to executives and customers
Comfort operating as a senior individual contributor, driving outcomes through prototyping and technical credibility

Preferred Qualifications:

Familiarity with multi-agent orchestration patterns (supervisor and sub-agent architectures, agent handoffs), which our use cases are likely to grow toward
Experience with our stack or comparable technologies: Node.js/TypeScript, PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, Kafka, AWS, Kubernetes
Experience leading AI-assisted or agentic development adoption across an engineering organization; given the scope of this work at SecurityScorecard, this carries significant weight
Experience partnering closely with data science or ML teams on productionizing their work
Cybersecurity industry background

Our Tech Stack

Our platform runs on Node.js and TypeScript, with a React Microfrontend Architecture and PostgreSQL and ClickHouse for storage. We use Kafka for event streaming, and our infrastructure runs on AWS with Kubernetes, Terraform, Helm, and ArgoCD. We are actively expanding our AI/ML infrastructure. You do not need to have used every tool here, but you should be comfortable reasoning across a stack of this kind and making principled architectural trade-offs within it.

Benefits:

Specific to each country, we offer a competitive salary, stock options, Health benefits, and unlimited PTO, parental leave, tuition reimbursements, and much more!
